Your portfolio is heavily weighted toward technology (26 %) and financials (18 %), with a moderate overall beta due to the core global ETFs. Key observations:

• **Technology**: 4 large-cap names (AAPL, NVDA, MSFT, AVGO) plus a small-cap (PLTR) and a high‑risk (IONQ). Exposure is high; the sector is volatile and sensitive to rate hikes and VIX swings.  
• **Financials**: 18 % concentration in banks and fintechs (BRK‑B, MSFT, IONQ). With the yield curve steepening negatively and credit spreads tightening, this sector could face margin pressure.  
• **Health Care, Industrials, Communication Services, Consumer Staples**: Under‑represented, offering defensive diversification.  
• **Risk profile**: High concentration in growth tech (MSFT, NVDA, AAPL) and a single defensive holding (BRK‑B). The portfolio’s beta is slightly above average (≈1.1) due to tech dominance and a negative yield‑curve slope that can compress valuations.  
• **Liquidity**: All holdings are liquid, but IONQ has a sharp decline (~‑19 %) and may be a candidate for removal or partial sale.  
• **Macro alignment**: Fed funds at 4.5 %, steepening curve, and rising oil support defense and industrials, but pressure on tech earnings.  
• **Suggested rebalancing**:  
  – Keep IWDA.AS and VWCE.DE for core diversification.  
  – Remove or reduce IONQ and PLTR due to poor performance and high volatility.  
  – Consider adding a higher‑conviction defense or industrial play (e.g., LMT) to replace HII and APP, maintaining a balanced tech/industrial mix.  
  – Re‑evaluate exposure to large-cap tech (AAPL, MSFT) – potential partial sell to reduce concentration.  

Overall, the portfolio is moderately diversified but leans too heavily on tech; adding a defense or utility tilt could improve risk‑adjusted returns.Your portfolio is moderately diversified with core global exposure from IWDA.AS and VWCE.DE.  
• **Sector concentration**: Technology (26 %) and Financials (18 %) dominate, leaving only 6 % in Consumer Staples and 9 % in Industrials.  
• **Risk profile**: High beta (~1.1) from tech names, plus a single defensive holding (BRK‑B). The negative yield‑curve slope and rising oil support defense but pressure on tech earnings.  
• **Liquidity**: All holdings are liquid; IONQ and PLTR are underperforming and highly volatile.  
• **Performance**: Current P&L shows modest gains in the core ETFs (+0.7 %) but significant losses in MSFT, IONQ, and PLTR.  
• **Recommendations**:  
  – **Keep** IWDA.AS, VWCE.DE, and AVGO to maintain core diversification.  
  – **Remove** IONQ and PLTR due to poor recent performance and high volatility.  
  – **Swap** HII for Lockheed Martin (LMT) to increase conviction in defense sector.  
  – **Add** a small position in a stable industrial like GE or a utility ETF to balance the tech tilt.  
  – **Re‑balance** the allocation to stay near the 2000 € budget, reducing the tech weight to ~20‑22 % and increasing defensive/utility exposure.
